_readme: Per-color enchantment glint behavior for Quark's runic etching, keyed by rune color name.
Reloads with F3+T. A color with no entry (or a missing field) behaves exactly like vanilla/Quark.
blend:  'vanilla' (default: glint squared, then added, like vanilla's) or 'tint' (2x multiply: below 50% gray
darkens and recolors the item, above 50% brightens it; can make genuinely dark glints).
texture: replace the glint texture. A bare name means lifeguard:textures/glint/<name>.png;
or give a full id like 'quark:textures/glint/enchanted_item_glint_red.png'. Omitted: lifeguard:textures/glint/<color>.png
if there is one (Dye Depot's colors have theirs there), else Quark's own.
colorize: tint only, 0 (default) to 1. A tint multiplies channel by channel, which rewrites an item's light
and dark: pixels already holding the tint's color stay bright, the rest go dark (orange on diamond:
the body goes dark, a few near-white highlights glare). Colorize gives each pixel the tint at its own
brightness instead, so the item keeps its shading and only changes color (its own hue, dyes
included, is replaced). 1 = fully colorized, in between mixes with the plain tint.
Works everywhere a rune glint shows: items, worn armor (trims included), elytra, shields (banner
patterns included) and tridents. Where it can't see the item (an unknown mod's renderer), a plain tint.
strength: tint only, 0 to 1 (default 1): how much the glint affects the item at all, fading toward the
untouched item. Use this, not a lower colorize, to tone a colorized glint down: lowering colorize mixes
the plain tint back in, and with it the uneven brightening colorize exists to avoid.
selective: tint only, 0 (default, off) or more: colorize only where the glint is strongly colored, fully at
this far from neutral gray (try 0.5). Near-neutral parts of the glint, meant to let the item show
through, then stay a plain multiply, keeping the item's own color instead of graying it.
ramp:   tint only, with colorize: colorize along a gradient instead of with one color, for a dye whose own shading
shifts hue (Dye Depot's tan: olive-brown shadows, peach mids, cream highlights). A list of up to 8 colors
('#RRGGBB'), each placed at its own brightness; the item's brightness picks the color. The texture is then
a gray ray map (black = field, white = heart of a ray; tools/glints mode 'ray'). Use with colorize 1.
Where it's drawn plain, the color's own tint texture (lifeguard:textures/glint/<color>.png) stands in for the ray map.
ramp_field: [low, high] (default [0, 1]): the stretch of the ramp an item's black to white spans in the field.
Narrow it to pull items into the ramp's middle (light items darken into the dye's mid-tones).
ramp_ray: [low, high] (default ramp_field): the same at the heart of a ray; higher lifts the item up the ramp.
vanilla: true = the rune draws vanilla's own glint, exactly: vanilla's render types in place of Quark's rune ones,
everywhere (items, armor, shaderpacks, resource packs). Every other setting is then ignored.
Under an Iris shaderpack every rune glint is plain Quark (these settings pause): Quark's own textures, and the
Quark-style ones the dye_depot_runes entry ships for Dye Depot's colors. Same with this entry (sexy_runic_glints) off.
